To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical-point shifts are in the range 0.5-2 K for the SF6-CP6 system.
pore condensation occurs just below Tc for the experimental system and that pore condensation also occurs in molecular dynamics simulations.
the critical temperature of a fluid in a pore is lower than the critical temperature of the bulk fluid, and that this shift is a function of the pore radius.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adsorption of a simple fluid in a mesoporous solid, where the pore radius is comparable to the size of the molecules.
the phase behaviour of fluids in pores.
the phase behaviour of fluids in mesoporous solids, and with the effects of confinement and surface forces on the phase behaviour of a confined fluid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the experimental results and the computer simulations are in good agreement with respect to the occurrence or absence of pore condensation and with respect to the dependence of the pore critical temperature on the radius.
pore condensation occurs for Tr > 0.95, but not at Tr = 1.0.
the pore condensation occurs when the fluid inside the pores is in the metastable region of the bulk phase behaviour.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phase behaviour of a confined fluid depends on its bulk properties, the pore radius R and the pore wall-fluid interaction.
the phase behaviour of a supercritical fluid in a mesopore is very different from that in the bulk.
the pore condensation phenomenon is strongly dependent on the fluid-fluid interaction, the pore size and the temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a pore critical temperature exists, but it is not accessible by the experimental methods used in this study.
pore condensation can occur at relative fugacities lower than the bulk saturation pressure if the pore is narrow enough.
the phase behaviour of a pore fluid is strongly influenced by the pore size and the fluid-fluid interaction.
